effort:high · full independent review with local build landed clean (sim lib 71 + all sim integration green; 9/9 corrected gouge pins + 55 rotated-envelope law tests + stock-source law suites; clippy clean; camcraft-app integration not run - main's #2244 wire_tool break blocks it, not this PR) · escalated: no

<!-- pr-reviewer: 465638b090038a13f82d85de848717f123fcf0aa -->

Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge. This review found no blocker.

## What looks good

- `stock_follow::sim_frame` is one law for the stock frame. `stock_sim::stock_grid`, `stock_sim_held::first_body` / `first_field` and `stock_view` all read it.
- A box turned by a quarter-turn multiple is modelled as its unturned twin. The new unit test checks the side swap about Z and the floor drop about X to 1e-9.
- A from-model stock is read from its placed mesh. The facets take the full transform, so no turn is ignored.
- An oblique box and a laid cylinder are refused by name (`OBLIQUE_STOCK`, `LAID_CYLINDER`). The refusal rides the post. Nothing passes in silence.
- `MoveModel` keeps the stock's own turn when the move does not turn the part. The pre-existing `turns` test (1e-12) is unchanged. The solve's float noise no longer lands on the stock.
- The UI says a refusal one time, in plain words. The uncut stock stays drawn. The new ui test pins both.

## The nine red tests from the last round

The author's answer is correct: the tests were the wrong device, not the code. Checks (a) to (d):

- (a) No production check was weakened. `SQUARE_TOL` stays 1e-9 and `is_square` is unchanged. The blanket "any rotation is refused" checks in `stock_sim.rs` and `stock_view.rs` are replaced by `sim_frame`, which still refuses every non-square turn by name. The `stock_follow.rs` hunk removes zero lines.
- (b) The fixture box check went from 1e-9 to 1e-4 mm in X and Y. The device turns the stock 1e-6 rad about Z; that moves the fixture corners by about 2.8e-5 mm. Z stays 1e-9. Judgement: this is fixture noise from the deliberate tiny turn, not a weakened assert. The box check is a fixture sanity check, not a gouge check.
- (c) The by_op asserts are kept. Every `assert_post_refused(.., rotated)` call site from the base is present at the head: 3 in `engrave_law`, 1 in `neighbour_law`, 2 in `stock_source_law`, plus the inline checks in `mark_floor`. Each by_op path now also asserts that the sim refuses the stock with `OBLIQUE_STOCK`. The device cannot become silent.
- (d) The move and the count are clean. `over_mcp_a_stock_source_cut_answers_for_the_part_the_same` moved word for word into `stock_source_law_mcp.rs`. The suite group goes 28 to 32. Test names at the merge base and at the head: none removed, 7 added. The four new suite tests are one `a_quarter_turned_stock_is_judged_by_the_program_sim` in each of `engrave_law`, `mark_floor`, `neighbour_law` and `stock_source_law`. The other three are `stock_in_vise_sim` (2 tests) and the `sim_frame` unit test. No coverage was lost. The added tests judge the quarter-turned stock and convict its gouge.

## Tests and build in this review

- The full diff was read. CRLF check: `git diff --numstat` equals `git diff -w --ignore-cr-at-eol --numstat` - no line-ending churn.
- Not built in this review. The merged tree cannot build at this time: `main` is red on `crates/app/src/mcp/wire_tool.rs` (#2244), and this PR does not touch that file. The app suites therefore did not run here.
- The author's gate row on this head is recorded in the body: the five law suites 32/32, `stock_in_vise_sim` 2/2, the shared-module suites green, and clippy `-p camcraft-app --all-targets -D warnings` clean. The prior review's merged run covered the predecessor head.

## Notes (not blocking)

- `stock_in_vise_sim` shares a fixture with PR #2184. Run the pair after the second of the two merges, as the body says.
- `docs/decisions/2177-square-stock-sim.md` records the sim_frame choice in the right place.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
